exposure: Mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: 843 women with a twin pregnancy ≥ 32 weeks (dichorionic or monochorionic diamniotic pregnancies) and a known pregnancy outcome from two European centers (Italy and Belgium)
finding: Neither the presentation of the second twin nor the chorionicity affected maternal and severe neonatal outcomes, regardless of the mode of delivery.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery (VD) was associated with poorer short-term neonatal outcomes compared to cesarean delivery, but severe adverse outcomes were similar between the two modes of delivery.
